scenarios.note: What libm returned for the five elementary functions the kit calls: sin, cos and tan over the angles its wrappers can produce, atan over the frustum's range and out to saturation, and pow over the damping grid ControlLoop.settle uses and the decimal registers' powers of a hundred. Grades the platform the TypeScript port delegates to, which is what measuring these samples settled (ADR 0022).
The whole decoded payload: craft parameters, control-loop rules, and every object, cell, surface structure and Room as the world builder resolved them.
What the player sees at the crash site the game opens on, looking north.
The same standing position turned 135 degrees, so a different set of cells is culled in.
Nose down from height, which puts the horizon and the ground fill in play together.
Rolled, so the ground fill leans and the lean transform is pinned with it.
An underground Room, drawn with its indoor backdrop rather than sky and ground.
A dark Room. Nothing is drawn at all, so this trace has no line records — which is the claim, not an omission.
The standard control handler, flown through a full circuit.
The player's first craft without a poweramp fitted, as the pair for the poweramp trace.
The one craft-conditioned bonus in the game: the same craft with a poweramp, which scales its throttle and lifts its ceiling.
The sinking handler, which has its own lift behaviour.
Craft slot 3, which dispatches through the standard handler. #66 asks for the flight trace per craft, so every boardable slot has one.
Craft slot 4, which dispatches through the standard handler. #66 asks for the flight trace per craft, so every boardable slot has one.
Craft slot 5, which dispatches through the sinking handler. #66 asks for the flight trace per craft, so every boardable slot has one.
Craft slot 6, which dispatches through the standard handler. #66 asks for the flight trace per craft, so every boardable slot has one.
Walking the surface on foot from the opening position: a stride, a turn on the spot, a stride while turning, a run, and a step of standing still.

The same mover underground, bounded by Room 3's walls without ever taking a Doorway: this gate ports Containment, while GameplaySession.traverse and DoorwayPredicate belong to the later session gate (#94).
A craft held level while the throttle sits on one notch, which is the mover without the circuit's feedback anywhere near it.
The opening script with no input at all. It plays its messages and parks in the routine that waits for a keypress, which is where a new game leaves it.

The same opening released by a keypress at twenty seconds, after which it runs on far enough to reach this trace's instruction limit and say so in its last record. The keypress is recorded as an input at the step it was applied, so a replay presses at the same step.

The same script with object 29's flag byte set, which its `tsto` test reads. It diverges on the seventh instruction and runs nine in total, stopping soonest of the four, so the three tests are pinned in the order the script applies them.

A script that draws a random byte, branches on it, and then ends on a jump to itself. The self-jump is why traces need an instruction limit: the interpreter spends its whole budget on that one jump every step, so this trace stops at its limit and says so in its last record.
The opening status report and purchase conversation, with the player answering the question it asks. This localized trace deliberately stops before walking or boarding.
Boarding by walking to the Dart and reaching for it, rather than by boarding from outside. This localized trace stops aboard the grounded craft.
The parity bar end to end: accept the 5,000-credit Dart purchase, walk and reach to board it, take off, fly to lift site 1 at grid 09:06, land, leave, walk onto the lift pad and descend into Room 1.
Walking into Room 127 from Room 144, which mirrors the world left for right. The trace shows the arrival and the flip on the same step.

The same Room entered from the other of its two ways in, and the world does not flip. Both of Room 127's stored alternates name Room 86, so arriving from 86 rewrites nothing — and the flip sits inside the branch that skips with it. That is PQ-0003, and since Room 127 has exactly two ways in it is half of that Room's observable behaviour.

A dark Room, whose header shows all three colours zeroed and nothing drawable (PQ-0004). The walk leaves it through the one Doorway that leads somewhere lit (Room 111) and comes back, so darkness is pinned turning off and on again rather than only at the start. Room 5's other two Doorways lead to Rooms 80 and 73, which are dark as well.
Walking into a locked Doorway empty-handed. The wall sounds and the player stays in Room 2: no arrival anywhere in this trace, which is the refusal.
The same Doorway carrying object 17, which is what it asks for. The Doorway opens and the walk carries on into Room 74 and beyond.

The Room that rewrites its own first Doorway by picking at random from eight destinations. On the default seed it picks Room 46; the seed is recorded in the header, so a different pick is a different scenario rather than a flaky trace.

retired.reason: Retired in #133. The Trace Oracle flew craft slot 7 through the standard control loop, integrating 47 frames of pitch input to altitude 8330 and landing it. The Reference Build's slot-7 handler at $AA62 does no such thing: at gameComplete 0 it writes $01 into the pitch high byte and returns, so the Interstellar Ship sits pinned a quarter turn nose-up and cannot be flown at all. The oracle is frozen and cannot re-emit this, so it is retired rather than re-recorded: Authoritative Evidence outranks it where the two disagree. The pinned handler is covered by web/test/mover.test.ts, which pins the attitude and proves it follows the decoded byte, and by the Escape route tests in web/test/escape.test.ts.

retired.reason: Retired in #131. These six traces exercised script 3's hand-in protocol through the `tsti` test, and the Trace Oracle emitted them with that opcode's polarity inverted: it answered "carried" where the Reference Build answers "not carried". The five listed here recorded the wrong branch and could not be reproduced by a correct interpreter. `script-3-flagged` is unaffected, because its `tsto` test exits before `tsti` runs, and it remains a live scenario. The oracle is frozen and cannot re-emit these, so they are retired rather than re-recorded: Authoritative Evidence outranks it where the two disagree. The predicate order they pinned is now covered by web/test/deliveries.test.ts.
